old_problem: The historical review treated the missing auxiliary-log selector and acceptance state as unresolved core intent. IPMI 2.0 section 31.12 defines the complete read-only command, the only three legal selectors, distinct MCA and OEM response layouts and unsupported behavior. Querying all legal selectors makes applicability discoverable without choosing or guessing one Project log in advance; only OEM semantic decoding and expected-state correlation remain bounded runtime inputs.
disposition_reason: Issue exactly one secret-safe OOB Storage 0Ah/5Ah query for each legal selector 00h, 01h and 02h. For MCA require the exact timestamp/count response and accept FFFFFFFFh only as the standardized unspecified-count sentinel. For OEM1/OEM2 require the exact timestamp/IANA/eight-status-byte framing and decode status only under the registered owner's versioned schema. Each type must end as validated supported, authoritative unsupported/N/A, or semantic NOT READY with raw evidence; reserved selectors are never probed. Preserve all logs and do not issue 5Bh, clear, injection, reset or mutation.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1202-1205, related IB row 1076, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests.json, tests_gpt_merged, manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The code occurs once in tests.json. The next formal queue identity was independently verified as row 1204 / variant 0e52013e574e83fd.

IPMI v2.0 Appendix G and section 31.12 assign Get Auxiliary Log Status to Storage NetFn 0Ah/Cmd 5Ah. The request contains exactly one Log Type byte with high nibble reserved zero and legal low-nibble values 00h MCA, 01h OEM1 and 02h OEM2; all others are reserved.

The standard requires an error completion when a requested log type is unsupported. Enumerating the three legal selectors once each therefore discovers the target's actual optional support without inventing a preferred subsystem or issuing a write.

MCA response data after completion is four-byte IPMI timestamp plus a 32-bit entry count, least-significant byte first. FFFFFFFFh explicitly means count unspecified and must be reported as such rather than decoded as 4,294,967,295 entries or FAIL.

OEM1/OEM2 response data after completion is four-byte timestamp, three-byte IANA Enterprise Number least-significant byte first, then exactly eight owner-defined status bytes. The standard defines framing but not status meaning; registered-owner and version-matched documentation is mandatory before semantic PASS.

A valid status response says that status metadata is readable; it does not by itself prove every underlying log entry is accessible or healthy. MCA count/time and OEM status must be correlated with the approved auxiliary-log producer, baseline or corresponding event context when a semantic expectation is claimed.

Unknown OEM schema does not require a new engineering decision about the command. The parser preserves raw IANA/status bytes and marks that type NOT READY FOR SEMANTIC PASS until the Project supplies its owner schema; it never guesses from BMC vendor name or another firmware.

Section 31.1 states Get is optional, and Set 5Bh cannot exist without Get while Get may exist alone. This case never infers Set support from successful Get and keeps row 1204 Set Auxiliary Log Status as an independent destructive identity.

The generic source step to clear logs is incompatible with a log-status read because it destroys the evidence and chronology being observed. The Review-layer command is read-only and explicitly preserves auxiliary, SEL, BMC and OS records.
OOB LANPlus target/session identity and secret handling are part of evidence. The related IB row 1076 cannot cross-credit this OOB Source Key even if returned bytes match.

ED-02 preserves identity; ED-03 separates standard framing from OEM meaning; ED-13 allows a standard BMC draft with parameters; ED-15 requires semantic criteria; ED-17 preserves logs; ED-19 separates IB/OOB; ED-28/ED-30 constrain recovery/approval; ED-33/ED-34 keep Master immutable while allowing bounded Project inputs; ED-38 prohibits hidden retry and DUT verdict claims.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Get Auxiliary Log Status (OOB Storage 0Ah/5Ah) complete MCA/OEM selector audit
test_case.purpose: Discover and validate every standard auxiliary-log status type exposed over the authenticated OOB interface, decode MCA metadata or owner-authorized OEM status without mutation, and report unsupported or semantically unready types explicitly while preserving the distinct IB and Set cases.
required_package: Verified BMC/SUT/firmware/IPMI identity and host-verified secret-safe LANPlus endpoint with credentials supplied outside process arguments
Pinned raw-command runner for Storage 0Ah/5Ah with one-shot per-selector execution, completion capture, exact response-length/reserved-bit/endian checks and redaction
IPMI timestamp decoder and MCA 32-bit count parser including FFFFFFFFh unspecified handling
IANA Enterprise Number registry mapping and, for each supported OEM type, the exact owner/firmware/version eight-byte status schema
Read-only auxiliary-log/SEL/BMC/OS evidence collector plus Project baseline or producer/event correlation for any asserted healthy/expected semantic state
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY OOB PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Verify BMC/SUT/firmware/channel and preserve auxiliary, SEL, BMC and OS evidence without clearing. Using host-verified secret-safe LANPlus, send exactly once for each selector: ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x5a 0x00, then 0x01, then 0x02; do not probe reserved values or retry automatically. For an unsupported error, preserve raw completion and map per target authority to N/A. For supported 00h require exactly eight response data bytes after completion: TS0..TS3 and COUNT0..COUNT3, decode little-endian timestamp/count and label FFFFFFFFh unspecified. For supported 01h/02h require exactly fifteen data bytes: TS0..TS3, IANA0..IANA2 and STATUS0..STATUS7; verify registered IANA and decode only with its versioned schema. Correlate each supported status with the approved underlying producer/baseline or corresponding event context. Report every selector independently as PASS, N/A/UNSUPPORTED, NOT READY FOR OEM SEMANTIC PASS or FAIL. Never issue 5Bh, clear/delete/acknowledge/inject logs, reset BMC or substitute row-1076 IB evidence.
test_case.expected_result: Each legal selector yields either an authority-mapped unsupported completion or a schema-exact response. MCA returns a valid/special IPMI timestamp and an LS-byte-first count or the explicit FFFFFFFFh unspecified sentinel. OEM returns a valid/special timestamp, registered IANA and eight status bytes decoded consistently with the exact owner schema; without that schema the raw result is retained as NOT READY, not guessed. Supported semantic values agree with the approved log baseline/producer context, all evidence remains unchanged, and no Set or clear operation occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS for the Source Key requires all three legal selectors accounted for: each supported type has exact response length/framing and its claimed semantic state is backed by MCA rules or an IANA-matched OEM schema and producer/baseline evidence; each unsupported type has authoritative completion evidence. FAIL covers reserved selector use, malformed length, bad endian/reserved data, unregistered/mismatched IANA used for a semantic claim, impossible status correlation, mutation, cleared evidence, wrong OOB target or concealed retry. NOT READY applies per OEM type when framing is valid but the eight-byte owner schema or expected context is absent. N/A is per-type and evidence-backed, never assumed because the platform is non-Itanium.
safety_gate: Read only over the verified OOB identity. Do not issue Set Auxiliary Log Status, SEL clear/delete, event injection, reset, power or any private write to discover meaning.
Do not execute the source boilerplate's log-clear step. Preserve the auxiliary log, SEL and correlated BMC/OS chronology needed to interpret timestamp/count/status.
Query only 00h, 01h and 02h with high nibble zero. Reserved selectors and missing selector bytes are invalid tests.

Validate completion and exact type-specific length before decoding. Treat unsupported completion as capability evidence only when mapped by standard/target authority; do not coerce it into empty healthy status.
Never decode OEM status without the returned IANA's exact versioned schema. Retain raw bytes and mark semantic readiness honestly.

One request per selector and no automatic retry. Timeout or malformed response is retained as first-failure evidence; later diagnostic collection requires a new run authorization and cannot overwrite it.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; BMC/SUT/firmware/OOB channel and secure-session identity; official 5Ah authority; distinct row-1076 IB and row-1204 Set identities
For each selector 00h/01h/02h: redacted exact request, timestamp, completion and full untruncated response with parser/tool version
MCA timestamp/count endian decode and explicit unspecified-sentinel handling, or unsupported authority
For each OEM response: timestamp, returned LS-first IANA, registry owner, schema/version provenance and field-by-field eight-byte interpretation or explicit semantic NOT READY
Auxiliary-log producer/baseline/event correlation, preserved SEL/BMC/OS evidence and no-mutation/no-log-clear audit
Per-selector PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A plus overall coverage statement and explicit confirmation that this review agent ran no DUT command
test_case.recovery: The case is read-only, so no state restoration is expected. On timeout, unsupported, malformed length, invalid timestamp/count or unknown OEM schema, preserve the first raw response and stop interpretation for that selector without retrying or probing reserved types. Verify no Set/Clear/Inject command was sent and that evidence stores remain unchanged; route schema or target anomalies to the auxiliary-log owner. Never mutate status or clear a log as a diagnostic workaround.

source_conflict.reason: Official section 31.12 resolves the TBD command, complete legal selector space, response layouts and unsupported behavior. The Review layer removes the evidence-clearing boilerplate and supplies exact OOB read-only acceptance without inventing OEM semantics.

blocked.reason: Command identity, selectors, standard MCA/OEM framing and unsupported handling are authoritative. Target identity, OEM schema and expected-state correlation are bounded runtime inputs; absence produces per-type NOT READY rather than an unresolved engineering operation.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Section 31.1 and section 31.12/Table 31-12 plus Appendix G define optional Storage 0Ah/Cmd5Ah, legal MCA/OEM1/OEM2 selectors, unsupported completion, MCA timestamp/count and OEM timestamp/IANA/eight-status-byte formats; section 31.13 defines the separate optional Set relationship.

project_authority: The auxiliary-log/BMC owner supplies target identity, maps unsupported completions, identifies the actual log producer and expected state, and provides IANA-matched OEM status documentation. It cannot authorize guessed OEM decoding, reserved selectors, log clearing, mutation, retry, IB substitution or a PASS based only on plausible bytes.
